Print/export Download as PDF Printable version In other projects Wikidata item Appearance move to sidebar hide From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia British actor (1937–1997) Jack Purvis Born ( 1937-07-13 ) 13 July 1937 London , England Died 21 November 1997 (1997-11-21) (aged 60) Bushey , Hertfordshire , England Occupation Actor Height 4 ft 2 in (1.27 m) [ 1 ] Jack Purvis (13 July 1937 – 21 November 1997) was a British actor. Purvis had dwarfism , and at 4 feet 2 inches (1.27 m) [ 1 ] was mainly cast in roles requiring actors of short stature. He appeared in three of filmmaker Terry Gilliam 's early fantasy films, with significant roles in Time Bandits and The Adventures of Baron Munchausen as well as a role in each film of the original trilogy in filmmaker George Lucas 's Star Wars . Career [ edit ] For twenty years until 1991, Purvis performed as part of a musical comedy double-act with Kenny Baker , billed as the "Mini-Tones" (Baker was also a dwarf). performed as part of a musical comedy double-act with Kenny Baker , billed as the "Mini-Tones" (Baker was also a dwarf). Purvis played the trumpet to Baker's mouth-organ and vibraphone. [ 2 ] The duo would attend auditions for Star Wars in 1976, where Baker was instantly cast as R2-D2 . At that time the duo had reached the final on the talent show Opportunity Knocks , and were reluctant to put the Mini-Tones work on hold. [ 3 ] After some negotiation, Purvis was also hired to appear in the film, [ 4 ] and would go on to play a different alien creature in each film of the original trilogy. [ 5 ] In 1991, Purvis became quadriplegic after his neck was broken in a car repair accident. [ 2 ] This and the 1990 death of David Rappaport led to Terry Gilliam 's indefinitely shelving an intended sequel to Time Bandits , where both actors played titular roles.
